result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually think and what they're willing to say to each other.

So much suffering seems to come from the performances we maintain—the carefully curated versions we show partners, colleagues, parents, strangers. The exhaustion of that. The loneliness of it. The way it calcifies into actual beliefs about who we are.

If people could be messier and more contradictory out loud without the social cost being so high, I think a lot would crack open. Not in a naive way—plenty of thoughts deserve pushback. But the chronic self-censoring, the performed confidence masking doubt, the hidden grief, the shameful wanting: that all poisons things quietly.

It wouldn't solve everything. People would still disagree, still hurt each other. But at least the hurt wouldn't come wrapped in mutual misunderstanding about what anyone actually thinks.
